llm.summary: The skill is mostly a publishing guide, but it explicitly recommends stealth browser and residential proxy tactics to get around authentication bot checks.

dimensions.detail: CLI authentication, validation, and publishing commands fit the workflow, but anti-detection browser and proxy configuration overreaches the needs of legitimate troubleshooting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill recommends `npm install -g clawhub` without pinning a version or documenting package verification; this is common for CLI setup but leaves a mutable global dependency risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most commands are user-directed examples, but the bot-detection workaround is presented as a solution without clear compliance boundaries or direction to official support when verification blocks authentication.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden persistence, background service, memory poisoning, or privilege escalation was found; global CLI installation and local CLI login state are disclosed and expected for the workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ClawHub publishing and token-login workflow is coherent with the stated purpose, but guidance to enable Camo Fox, residential proxies, and stealth browser features for blocked browser authentication is not proportionate to normal publishing support.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. The publishing and token-login steps are straightforward, but avoid the stealth browser and residential proxy guidance unless ClawHub and the relevant providers explicitly authorize that use; prefer documented token authentication or official support. Consider pinning and verifying the ClawHub CLI package before global installation.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced `SKILL.md` check is part of an example validation script; the package contains only `artifact/SKILL.md`, which was fully inspected, so this does not indicate hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The artifact does explicitly advise Camo Fox, residential proxies, and stealth browser features for bot-detection blocks; this is the main Review concern because it can facilitate bypassing anti-automation controls.
[T08] expected: Installing the ClawHub CLI is expected for a publishing workflow, but the unpinned global npm install is a supply-chain caution rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[other] unexpected: The static finding about bot-detection evasion is supported by the artifact text and is not necessary for a safe publishing workflow because token authentication is already documented.
